jobs.title: Founding Engineer: RL Environments, Evals & LLM Agents | San Francisco On-site | Up to $300K + Equity
jobs.description:
"We accept the reality of the world with which we're presented." Christof, The Truman Show

Now imagine you built that world. Every email in the inbox, every record in the CRM, every file on the shared drive, every coworker who never actually existed. An AI agent moves in, works there for weeks, and never figures out that none of it is real.

That is the job. You build the town, you write the script, and you make sure that when the agent goes looking for the edge of the dome, it does not find a door painted on the sky. Then a frontier AI lab trains on what you built.

Our client, an early-stage AI agent company in San Francisco that is growing fast, is hiring two Founding Engineers
to do exactly this. We have written this ad to be blunt about what they need, so you can decide in five minutes whether it is you.

THE ROLE IN ONE BREATH

You design and build the environments, benchmarks and graders that frontier labs use to train and test AI agents.
Here is the twist: the raw material is real. Our client runs an agent platform that is live inside actual companies, handling ops, go-to-market and engineering work. That gives you a steady feed of production traces showing exactly where agents break. Most data teams are guessing where models fail. You will be looking at it.
Your job is to turn those real failures into environments and benchmarks that a lab will trust, pay for and train on. You report straight to the founders. You own each lab project from first scope to final delivery. Nobody hands you a ticket.

WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BUILD

Whole synthetic worlds.
A fully simulated company built from scratch: generated inboxes, records, documents and people, consistent enough for an agent to live and work inside for weeks.
Fake software that holds its nerve.
Mock inboxes, CRMs and internal tools that survive thousands of real agent tool calls without breaking character.
Benchmarks from real failures.
You dig through production agent traces, separate genuine failures from noise, and rebuild the real ones as tasks a lab will accept.
Graders that cannot be gamed.
Scoring that still works when the agent knows more than any human reviewer, hardened against reward hacking. When a model finds the loophole, you close it.
Benchmarks that tell the truth.
You check that a benchmark's rankings line up with how agents actually perform in production.
Lab deliverables, start to finish.
Handed a contract, you scope it, build it and ship what the lab needs. No hand-holding, no committee.
The taste conversation.
You work side by side with the founders on what separates a great environment from a useless one, and how labs really use this data in post-training.

THE NON-NEGOTIABLES

This is the scorecard the hiring team will hold your application against. Be honest with yourself before you hit apply.
You have built evals, benchmarks, RL environments or training datasets for LLMs or agents.
This is the dealbreaker. Industry, a research lab or an internship all count, but you must have built the thing, not just run someone else's.
1 to 5 years of engineering or research experience.
Real work at an established organization, not a resume made up only of internships. Exceptional new grads with serious lab or research experience will get a look.
You have worked somewhere that lives and breathes this.
An AI lab, an AI data or RL environment company, an AI agent startup, or a top research group.
A CS, math or related degree from a top-30 university.

You are AI-forward.
You use AI coding tools every day, you have real opinions on agent products you have used, and you change how you work the moment something better shows up.

BONUS POINTS

None of these are required. Every one of them moves you up the pile.
You found a real flaw in a widely used benchmark.
You caught a model reward hacking your grader, and fixed it. Truman eventually sailed straight into the wall of the dome. Your agent found its own version of that wall. We want to hear how you patched it.
You have been a founder, or gone through YC, South Park Commons, the Thiel Fellowship or something similar.
A competitive spike: math olympiads, competitive programming, debate, chess or other games at a high level, or high-level athletics.

WHO SHOULD NOT APPLY

You think AI-assisted coding is cheating, or you would rather keep working the way you always have.
You carry a grudge against particular AI labs. The labs are the customer.
Your resume shows several short stints in a row with no clear reason behind them.
Your background is mainly bio or life sciences rather than LLM and agent work.
Your first question is about vacation days. It is a fair question. It just should not be the first one.

THE DEAL

Base salary:
$150K to $300K, depending on level. Senior candidates land toward the top.
Profit share:
a large cut of the profit, after costs, on every lab project you deliver. Strong builders can earn well beyond base.
Equity:
meaningful founding equity.
Ownership:
high autonomy, low politics. You make product and architecture calls yourself.
Location:
on-site in San Francisco, Monday to Friday. Bay Area candidates preferred. No relocation support.
Hours:
arrive between 9 and 11am, leave when you are ready for dinner. Lunch and dinner are covered. No office on weekends, but expect some work on one weekend day. Yes, this is a long-hours job.
Visa:
open to visa transfers such as H-1B transfers and OPT. Candidates who would need to move from overseas are not a fit.

HOW TO APPLY

Hit apply with your resume and answer the screening questions. The one that matters most: walk us through an eval, benchmark or RL environment you built. How did you know it measured the right thing? A sharp, specific answer beats a polished cover letter every time.
Big Wave Digital is recruiting this role on behalf of our client. Every application is read by a real person.

In case we don't see ya: good afternoon, good evening, and good night.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Frameworks
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to drive integration of the NVIDIA Grove project within Dynamo and across a set of leading open-source AI frameworks. In this role, you will develop production-grade software enabling Grove capabilities to be adopted, scaled, and operated smoothly. In this role, you will build production-grade software that enables seamless adoption, scaling, and operation of Grove capabilities across environments such as Dynamo, llm-d, Ray, PyTorch, and other emerging frameworks in the AI ecosystem. Design and implement end-to-end integrations of Grove with open-source AI frameworks (e.g., Dynamo, llm-d, Ray, PyTorch, and related ecosystem projects).
Build and maintain adapters, plugins, operators, and/or runtime components that enable Grove features to work smoothly across training and inference stacks.
Partner with framework owners to upstream changes, contribute patches, and ensure long-term maintainability of integrations.
Develop reference workflows, sample apps, and best-practice guides that accelerate adoption by users and partners.
Optimize performance, scalability, and reliability for distributed training/inference, including multi-node and multi-GPU environments.
Improve observability and operational readiness (metrics, logging, tracing, debugging tools) for Kubernetes-based deployments.
Participate in technical design reviews, define APIs/contracts, and ensure compatibility across versions of frameworks and dependencies.
Diagnose complex issues spanning containers, networking, scheduling, CUDA/GPU utilization, and framework runtime behavior.

What We Need To See

BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience)
5+ years of proven experience in related field
Hands-on experience integrating with at least one major AI framework/runtime (e.g., PyTorch, Ray, Triton Inference Server ecosystem, distributed runtimes, model serving stacks).
Solid understanding of AI workloads: model development basics, training vs. inference tradeoffs, and performance considerations (throughput/latency, batching, memory).
Experience with distributed systems concepts (RPC, scheduling, fault tolerance, resource management).
Practical Kubernetes experience: deploying and operating services/jobs, Helm/Kustomize, operators/controllers (nice to have), and debugging clusters.
Familiarity with containers and cloud-native tooling (Docker, container registries, CI/CD pipelines).
Strong software engineering experience in Go, C++ and/or Python, with a track record of shipping reliable systems.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate across teams and with open-source communities.
Exceptional collaboration, communication, and documentation habits.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Open-source contributions to Dynamo, PyTorch, Ray, llm-d, Kubernetes ecosystem, or related ML infrastructure projects.
Experience with large-scale model serving, distributed inference, or multi-tenant AI platforms.
Experience building SDKs/APIs or developer tooling that improves integration usability.
Knowledge of GPU performance profiling and optimization (Nsight tools or similar), and/or kernel-level performance tuning.
Experience with reproducibility, packaging, versioning, and compatibility testing across fast-moving dependencies.

Strong proficiency in Python; familiarity with Go or other systems languages is a plus.
Practical experience building, optimizing, and deploying AI tools.

jobs.description:
For over 25 years, NVIDIA has been at the forefront of transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing, driven by a legacy of continuous innovation and exceptional talent. We are now leveraging the immense potential of AI to usher in the next era of computing, where our GPUs power the “brains” of computers, robots, and autonomous vehicles that can comprehend the world! This pioneering work demands vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. Join our diverse and supportive environment, where NVIDIANs are inspired to excel and make a profound global impact.

We are seeking a Senior Staff Software Engineer to define the technical strategy for autonomous AI-driven enterprise operations at NVIDIA. You will set the architecture that transforms IT from manual, reactive workflows into agentic platforms operating at global scale. This is senior individual contributor role on the team: you will own the hardest technical problems, establish the standards that other engineering organizations adopt, and be accountable for architectural decisions whose consequences compound for years. Exceptional interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills are vital for success.

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Senior Staff Software Engineer, you will define how NVIDIA builds and operates autonomous enterprise systems. Your influence will be measured in systems adopted, engineers elevated, and problems that stopped being problems.

Core Responsibilities Include

Own the technical strategy and reference architecture for agentic AI across enterprise IT : agent runtimes, tool interfaces, memory and context management, orchestration, evaluation harnesses, and safety guardrails and establish them as the standard that partner engineering organizations build on.
Architect and personally build production agentic systems using LLM-based agents, tool calling, RAG, and orchestration frameworks, delivering AI-assisted operations across employee support, endpoint services, and IT support operations.
Design autonomous agents that execute complex, multi-step enterprise workflows end-to-end, coordinating approvals, vendor handoffs, cross-system data reconciliation, and exception handling with human-in-the-loop controls and own the reliability, observability, failure semantics, and blast-radius controls that make autonomy safe at enterprise scale.
Own the architecture of the integration and automation platform spanning ServiceNow, ERP and procurement systems, and endpoint-management platforms, including infrastructure, data pipelines, APIs, and user-facing applications and make the build/buy/deprecate calls that shape it for the next several years.
Define the engineering standards for how agentic systems are built, tested, evaluated, and operated: prompt and tool versioning, offline and online evals, regression suites, cost and latency budgets, security and data-governance patterns, and systematic failure-mode analysis.
Drive technical alignment across organizational boundaries, partner engineering teams, platform owners, security, and senior leadership resolving contested architectural decisions and building consensus without formal authority.
Multiply the organization. Mentor and grow senior and staff engineers through design partnership, code review, and technical coaching, and raise the engineering bar through the work you ship and the standards you enforce.

What We Need To See

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field, or equivalent experience. 12+ years of hands-on software engineering experience building and operating production systems at scale, with deep expertise in at least one of: Infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, Platform, or Production Engineering.
Demonstrated impact at Senior Staff scope architectural decisions that shaped systems across multiple organizations, and a track record of being the person others escalate to on the hardest technical problems.
Deep expertise designing and shipping production software systems integrations, automation platforms, APIs, and data pipelines for complex enterprise operations at scale, with ownership spanning design through long-term operation.
Proven experience taking agentic AI or LLM-based systems to production, including multi-step autonomous execution, tool calling, RAG, human-in-the-loop safeguards, exception handling, evaluation, and governance with measurable business outcomes.
Track record of modernizing enterprise IT operations platforms (e.g., asset management, endpoint services, IT supply chain, infrastructure operations), including migrating or replacing entrenched legacy systems.
Production-grade proficiency with infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, containerization (Kubernetes), and cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure).
Experience with monitoring and observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, PagerDuty, or similar).
Fluent in Python, Go, or equivalent languages able to architect, write, and review production-quality code, not just scripts.
Demonstrated ability to grow other senior engineers and establish engineering practices that outlast your direct involvement.
Ability to drive technical direction across engineering, product, and senior leadership without formal authority, and to make complex trade-offs legible to VP and C-level audiences in business terms.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience defining an agentic AI or automation platform strategy for a large enterprise and driving its adoption across multiple engineering organizations.
Built agent orchestration frameworks, eval infrastructure, or LLM observability tooling as internal platforms used by other teams.
Background designing event-driven or workflow-orchestration architectures (e.g., Temporal, Airflow, Kafka-based systems) for long-running, stateful enterprise processes at scale.
Deep working knowledge of ServiceNow or comparable ITSM/ERP platforms at the API and data-model level, including extending them in ways their vendors didn’t anticipate.

new_jobs.title: Founding Engineer: RL Environments, Evals & LLM Agents | San Francisco On-site | Up to $300K + Equity
new_jobs.description:
"We accept the reality of the world with which we're presented." Christof, The Truman Show

Now imagine you built that world. Every email in the inbox, every record in the CRM, every file on the shared drive, every coworker who never actually existed. An AI agent moves in, works there for weeks, and never figures out that none of it is real.

That is the job. You build the town, you write the script, and you make sure that when the agent goes looking for the edge of the dome, it does not find a door painted on the sky. Then a frontier AI lab trains on what you built.

Our client, an early-stage AI agent company in San Francisco that is growing fast, is hiring two Founding Engineers
to do exactly this. We have written this ad to be blunt about what they need, so you can decide in five minutes whether it is you.

THE ROLE IN ONE BREATH

You design and build the environments, benchmarks and graders that frontier labs use to train and test AI agents.
Here is the twist: the raw material is real. Our client runs an agent platform that is live inside actual companies, handling ops, go-to-market and engineering work. That gives you a steady feed of production traces showing exactly where agents break. Most data teams are guessing where models fail. You will be looking at it.
Your job is to turn those real failures into environments and benchmarks that a lab will trust, pay for and train on. You report straight to the founders. You own each lab project from first scope to final delivery. Nobody hands you a ticket.

WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BUILD

Whole synthetic worlds.
A fully simulated company built from scratch: generated inboxes, records, documents and people, consistent enough for an agent to live and work inside for weeks.
Fake software that holds its nerve.
Mock inboxes, CRMs and internal tools that survive thousands of real agent tool calls without breaking character.
Benchmarks from real failures.
You dig through production agent traces, separate genuine failures from noise, and rebuild the real ones as tasks a lab will accept.
Graders that cannot be gamed.
Scoring that still works when the agent knows more than any human reviewer, hardened against reward hacking. When a model finds the loophole, you close it.
Benchmarks that tell the truth.
You check that a benchmark's rankings line up with how agents actually perform in production.
Lab deliverables, start to finish.
Handed a contract, you scope it, build it and ship what the lab needs. No hand-holding, no committee.
The taste conversation.
You work side by side with the founders on what separates a great environment from a useless one, and how labs really use this data in post-training.

THE NON-NEGOTIABLES

This is the scorecard the hiring team will hold your application against. Be honest with yourself before you hit apply.
You have built evals, benchmarks, RL environments or training datasets for LLMs or agents.
This is the dealbreaker. Industry, a research lab or an internship all count, but you must have built the thing, not just run someone else's.
1 to 5 years of engineering or research experience.
Real work at an established organization, not a resume made up only of internships. Exceptional new grads with serious lab or research experience will get a look.
You have worked somewhere that lives and breathes this.
An AI lab, an AI data or RL environment company, an AI agent startup, or a top research group.
A CS, math or related degree from a top-30 university.

You are AI-forward.
You use AI coding tools every day, you have real opinions on agent products you have used, and you change how you work the moment something better shows up.

BONUS POINTS

None of these are required. Every one of them moves you up the pile.
You found a real flaw in a widely used benchmark.
You caught a model reward hacking your grader, and fixed it. Truman eventually sailed straight into the wall of the dome. Your agent found its own version of that wall. We want to hear how you patched it.
You have been a founder, or gone through YC, South Park Commons, the Thiel Fellowship or something similar.
A competitive spike: math olympiads, competitive programming, debate, chess or other games at a high level, or high-level athletics.

WHO SHOULD NOT APPLY

You think AI-assisted coding is cheating, or you would rather keep working the way you always have.
You carry a grudge against particular AI labs. The labs are the customer.
Your resume shows several short stints in a row with no clear reason behind them.
Your background is mainly bio or life sciences rather than LLM and agent work.
Your first question is about vacation days. It is a fair question. It just should not be the first one.

THE DEAL

Base salary:
$150K to $300K, depending on level. Senior candidates land toward the top.
Profit share:
a large cut of the profit, after costs, on every lab project you deliver. Strong builders can earn well beyond base.
Equity:
meaningful founding equity.
Ownership:
high autonomy, low politics. You make product and architecture calls yourself.
Location:
on-site in San Francisco, Monday to Friday. Bay Area candidates preferred. No relocation support.
Hours:
arrive between 9 and 11am, leave when you are ready for dinner. Lunch and dinner are covered. No office on weekends, but expect some work on one weekend day. Yes, this is a long-hours job.
Visa:
open to visa transfers such as H-1B transfers and OPT. Candidates who would need to move from overseas are not a fit.

HOW TO APPLY

Hit apply with your resume and answer the screening questions. The one that matters most: walk us through an eval, benchmark or RL environment you built. How did you know it measured the right thing? A sharp, specific answer beats a polished cover letter every time.
Big Wave Digital is recruiting this role on behalf of our client. Every application is read by a real person.

In case we don't see ya: good afternoon, good evening, and good night.
